summary: A satirical essay lamenting the decline of soft skills in a technically driven workplace, covering the loss of water cooler chat, emoji-free emails, spreadsheet-based leadership and obsolete teamwork. It introduces a fictional 'Sarcasm as a Service' training program by CEO Oscar Irony and cites sociologist Dr. Lucille Chatfield's prediction that soft skills will return. It closes by urging readers to value emotional intelligence and human connection.
one_line: A humorous satirical essay on the decline of workplace soft skills in a technical economy and the hope of their revival.
key_facts: The essay is set around October 17th, 2023, and portrays workplace empathy and interpersonal skills as nearly extinct.
The essay claims water cooler banter has been replaced by algorithms and apps; Bob from accounting no longer shares vacation photos with Sally from HR because 'There's an app for that.'
The last smiley face was supposedly seen in a professional email in early September 2023.
'Sarcasm as a Service' is a training program spearheaded by CEO Oscar Irony and launched on November 12th, 2023.
Oscar Irony's program aims to turn sterile office exchanges into witty quips and clever retorts, including playful but constructive barbs in boardrooms.
By December 1st, 2023, the essay imagines job advancement depending only on technical skills such as fluency in C++ and Python.
In the essay's hard-skills world, conflict resolution is jokingly replaced by rock-paper-scissors.
Modern supervisors are described as relying on spreadsheets, analytics tools, graphs and pie charts instead of mentoring or pep talks.
Team-building retreats have been replaced by silent coworking spaces where the most interaction is a shared printer.
Sociologist Dr. Lucille Chatfield argues the pendulum will swing back as the market realizes robots cannot manage a team building exercise as humans do.
Luke, the intern, is quoted: 'An office without laughter is a spreadsheet with no data.'
The essay concludes that human connection and emotional intelligence hold immeasurable value despite the importance of technical expertise.
